newsitem.title: USA: Producers eye coastal tracts in Texas lease sale.
newsitem.headline: Producers eye coastal tracts in Texas lease sale.

text.p: More than one million acres of Texas land divided into 2,390 tracts will be up for auction in the October oil and natural gas lease sale, the Texas School Land Board said on Wednesday.

The number of tracts nominated for inclusion in the lease round rose 16 percent from the last sale in April on surging interest in exploration and production in the state, Texas Land Commissioner Garry Mauro said in a statement.
"Our lease sales are a bellwether of the energy industry and all indications are for continued growth in exploration for natural gas along the coast," he said.

In the October 7 lease sale, bids will be taken on 1,444 tracts covering 757,550 acres in state waters of the Gulf of Mexico, 812 tracts covering 282,340 acres in state bay waters and 46 river tracts and 39 inland tracts covering 6,619 acres.
The Texas land office manages 13.3 million acres of state lands and mineral rights, and proceeds from the leases are deposited into the state's Permanent School Fund.
